question: In which year was the first Arjuna Award given to a woman hockey player?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1961**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **first woman hockey player** to receive the Arjuna Award was **Anne Lumsden in 1961.**
 
• It is bestowed by the Government of India (Ministry of Youth Affairs and sports) to sportspersons for their outstanding performance in international
 
 
• as well as national events and also holds leadership qualities with good morals.
 
 
 
• The award was launched in 1961 with a cash prize of Rs 5 lakh, a bronze statue of Arjuna, and
 
 
• a scroll and is presented by the President of India every year to the sportspersons of different categories. 
 
 
 
• Now the Prize money is increased to 15 lakhs.
 
• The honour is named on Prince Arjuna, the protagonist of the Indian epic Mahabharata.
 
• He must have shown qualities of leadership sportsmanship and a sense of discipline.
 
• From 2001, the award is given in disciplines falling under the following categories: 
 
 
• Olympic Games/Commonwealth Games/Asian Games
 
• World Cup/World Championship disciplines and cricket;
 
• Indigenous games; and
 
• Sports for the physically challenged.
 
 
 
• The Arjuna Award was first presented in 1961 to six people.
 
• Meena Shah (Badminton) was the first woman to get the Arjuna award in 1962.
 
• The first recipient of the Arjuna Award in the field of Archery was Krishna Das awarded in 1961.
